chapter_theme: Creation (படைத்தல்): from the beginningless Supreme come Shakti, nada and bindu, and from bindu, as Maya, the tattvas, elements and worlds. The gods who create and keep the worlds act within this order; the Lord alone, with his Shakti, is said to create, protect and remove the worlds and to be their life.
structure_note: The chapter opens with the pure order of manifestation (381 to 385: Supreme, Shakti, nada, bindu, the elements), turns to the Lord and Shakti as the pair who create through the gods of the five acts (386 to 403), sums up in the refrain verses on the one who creates, protects and removes (404, 407), and ends with the Lord as the eighty-four lakh kinds of life and with everything as born of bindu (409, 410).

381.reading: The supreme beyond the supreme, without beginning or end, unites as knowledge with its consort power; as light spreads in that, the flawless Para appears, and from her nada shines.
381.nuance: பராபரம் and பராபரை are a male and female pair, traditionally Siva and his Shakti; the variant பராபரன் makes the first explicitly personal. The order Supreme, Shakti, Para, nada is the tradition's sequence of pure manifestation; the verse states it compactly and the steps are not fixed by it alone.

382.reading: In nada is bindu, and in nada and bindu Siva and Shakti come within, flawless; as they divide, knowledge and action are born, and bindu rises out of the will that impels them.
382.nuance: ஞானம், கிரியை and இச்சை are traditionally Shakti's three powers of knowing, acting and willing. வாதித்த (impelling, or arguing) is unusual here.

383.reading: What was not comes to be in Shakti's place and stays mingled within like light in a gem; that Being which opened the way for it to become mighty is, if one tries to put it into words, farther than far.
383.nuance: இல்லது can mean 'what does not exist' or 'what has no abode'; the reading turns on it. கல்லொளி, light in a stone or gem, is an image of presence that is inside yet unmixed. The last line is plain: the source is beyond speech.

384.reading: From that farness the light becomes a Shakti, nada joins with longing and becomes a bindu, and Sadasiva becomes the support of the five beginning with earth, with Shakti as their binding.
384.nuance: சாத்துமான் at the end is obscure; I take it loosely as 'that which binds or holds'. The five from earth are the elements. The verse continues 383's தூராதி தூரமே by opening with தூரத்தில்.

385.reading: In mahat space arises and air grows, water mingles and hardens, the five crowd together and become the five elements, and standing in the flower the worlds take form.
385.nuance: மான் is taken as mahat, the great tattva, and the verse as the usual chain of elements from space to earth; கான் (forest, or fire) and தேன் (honey) are hard to fit to that chain and may be corrupt or symbolic. பூ may be the earth or Brahma's lotus.

386.reading: One He and one She create the world; those who create it have five sons; the creator is also the one seated on the flower, and the one who creates the world is that holy one himself.
386.nuance: The five sons are traditionally the five lords of the five acts (Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Maheshvara, Sadasiva). The verse repeats புவனம் படைப்பான் four times: creation is credited to the pair, to Brahma and to the holy one, and the last line gathers them into one.

387.reading: The holy Nandi, joined with the Shakti who nurtures cool mahat in every world, in union wholly by nature of the eye, blossoms in the flower of earth's nature.
387.nuance: கண்ணியல்பாக and மண்ணியல்பாக are paired but unclear; the sense of Siva and Shakti together flowering into the world is clear, the details are not.

388.reading: In water pleasure is born, in fire light in the body, in air the sounding power of good life's breath, and between water and earth the state of birth.
388.nuance: The verse seems to match elements to qualities (taste, form, sound, smell) and to the body, but its lines do not give a clean scheme; the variant காய்கதிர் for காயத்திற் would make 'the burning sun's light' instead of 'light in the body'.

389.reading: With the one who swallowed and spat out the seven worlds, with the head of the gods and the first one, and with the four-faced cause, it is that Being who of old creates this world.
389.nuance: The one who swallowed the worlds is Vishnu in his familiar myth, the four-faced one Brahma. The verse makes them companions of the creator, not the creator; whether அண்டத்தமரர் தலைவன் and ஆதி are Rudra or the Lord himself is unclear.

390.reading: With the sky that lies within the vast ocean, the Supreme of Kailasa, and Brahma above on the swelling lotus, he knew how life is placed there.
390.nuance: The three figures are usually taken as Vishnu (the one in the ocean), Siva of Kailasa and Brahma; the subject of உணர்ந்தானே is not named.

391.reading: The Cause stands everywhere, mingled in love; Narayana stands as the middle body; the four-faced one, from love of the Lord of the world, shapes its parts and is settled as the world of the Veda.
391.nuance: காரணன், நாரணன், பாரணன் and ஆரணம் chime. பதஞ்செய்யும் may mean 'makes ready' or 'makes the stations'; நடுவுடல் (middle body) is obscure.

392.reading: There is a Lord whose kindness is easy to reach, who makes the great gem yield its fruit with ease; staying there as Brahma's light he creates, and I have understood clearly the easy way to the fruit.
392.nuance: பருமாமணி (great gem) and அயஒளி (Brahma's light, or the light of the unborn) are not fixed by the verse. எளிது (easy) is said three times; the point that the Lord is easy of access is plain.

393.reading: When the pure one in grace grants going and coming, and growth becomes thought, the merciful one himself strikes and stirs the eight directions that stand high.
393.nuance: போக்கும் வரவும, going and coming, is commonly taken as death and birth. Calling the one who stirs the directions தயாபரன், the supremely merciful, makes the stirring itself an act of grace.

394.reading: The spotless one who makes life stands in the middle: he measures my precious life into one life to fit a body, is help to the body that brings earlier suffering, and makes the life good.
394.nuance: முன்துயர் (earlier suffering) may be the karma that the body brings with it. நடுவு நின்றான் may mean 'stood within' or 'stood impartial'.

395.reading: In making things become, the Lord who wears bone beads and konrai, with a body adorned like burning red gold, enters the departing soul and is there as its body; he is the master who works becoming.
395.nuance: அக்கணி is taken as அக்கு அணி, wearing bone or rudraksha beads, and the konrai flower and red-gold body are Siva's marks. போகின்ற சீவன் may be the soul leaving one body for the next.

396.reading: One He and one She have set to play; the play of the two brings forth everything, many fruits in every season, and the work in one Tiru becomes the whole world.
396.nuance: திரு is commonly taken as Shakti, so that the world is her work; it could also be read as fortune or holiness. விளையாடல் makes creation play, not labour or need.

397.reading: The Lord of the worlds enters and knows, the lord with the discus enters and knows, the god on the flower enters and knows; they stand as those who enter and know up to the crown.
397.nuance: The three are usually Rudra, Vishnu and Brahma. The last line is obscure: முடிக்காகி may mean they know only so far, below the summit, which would set limits on these gods.

398.reading: The power of anava and the five within it, the lords of effect and cause in their order, born of bindu through the five acts they tend, can be called those from whom anava has not left.
398.nuance: ஆணவம் is the root impurity of Siddhanta. The verse's claim, as I read it, is that the five lords who carry out the five acts are themselves still bound souls, not the Lord: a strong ranking of the gods below Siva.

399.reading: Of the three parts that came, one is the rising of Maya; the other three are bindu risen from Maya; since nada, which begot it, is born of Para, this is the ancient play of the supreme Siva.
399.nuance: The count (three parts, one, then 'the other three') does not add up as read; a word may be lost or முப்பால் may be meant differently. The variant பெற்றவள் makes the begetter female.

400.reading: Space and the rest, and Sadasiva and the others, went out together within the unfailing Shakti: the great-bodied Isa, Hara, Mal and Brahma, so that space and earth are cared for.
400.nuance: The last line is unclear; with the variant அளித்ததே it would say that this is what gave space and earth.

401.reading: In the gracious triangle born of bindu she is Tripura; she settles as Sadasiva, and she performs the five acts.
401.nuance: அளியார், repeated at each line's head, may mean 'full of grace' or 'like bees'. முக்கோணம் (triangle) and வயிந்தவம் (born of bindu) suggest a yantra. Here the five acts are hers, where 404 gives them to the One.

402.reading: Manonmani with banded breasts, the auspicious one, mingled as cause and effect; she of the Veda, enchantress of the gods, the full one, is also the knowing at the root of all knowing.
402.nuance: A string of names of the goddess. With the variant பூதாதி the last line reads 'source of the elements' rather than 'knowing at the root of knowing'.

403.reading: He agreed to be these: Maheshvara who stands full as himself, Hara and Tirumal who go and move there, and Brahma on the flower who makes.
403.nuance: The gods are one Lord's forms, as the verse says, but மன்றது செய்யும் for Brahma is unclear.

404.reading: One alone created the seven worlds, one alone protected them, one alone wiped them away, and one alone is the life with the worlds.
404.nuance: The fourfold ஒருவனுமே insists on one agent where the chapter elsewhere names several gods and a Shakti. The variant உடலோடுயிர் makes the last line 'the life with the body'.

405.reading: Our Lord, red-lotus coloured, fire coloured and dark as the rain cloud, stands having cut off the birth that comes in Maya's bond and in union with women of flowered hair.
405.nuance: The three colours are commonly matched to Brahma, Rudra and Vishnu, all as the one Lord. The variant last line ஐந்தார் பிறவி அமைத்து நின்றானே says the opposite: that he set up five-fold birth. In a chapter on creation the variant fits as well as the received text.

406.reading: The great Nandi, who made the nature of the births in which soul, body and life come together in all eight directions people search, stands within those who seek him, and I know their way of seeking.
406.nuance: ஊடும் may mean 'who sulk with him' or 'who pass through', so 'those who seek' is a guess. The verse recurs almost word for word as 414.

407.reading: One host creates the seven worlds, one host protects them, one host wipes them away, and one host is the life with the worlds.
407.nuance: The verse repeats 404 with ஓராயமே in place of ஒருவனுமே. ஆயம் can mean a company or a gathering, so the agent may be the Lord's assembled powers; tradition differs on the word, and it may be a corruption of 404's line.

408.reading: The one Lord and the good two kneaded beings together with the dross of their kinds; to the two who stand ready asking what their task is, he, the first, gives grace.
408.nuance: The two are usually taken as Brahma and Vishnu, and கோது குலம் as the impure classes of beings. The verse is compressed and the reading is tentative.

409.reading: In that way he spreads truly as life in eighty-four lakh kinds; to men who talk falsely he stands covered by darkness.
409.nuance: The eighty-four lakh kinds of birth are a common count, also in the Tevaram, as Sengalvaraya notes. மெய்ப்பரிசு and பொய்ப்பரிசு play true against false manner: the Lord is present in all life, yet hidden from the false.

410.reading: Sun, moon, fire, the eight guardians, sky with its sound, water and earth, the contending qualities beginning with sound, speech, mind and the rest all come from the bindu of Maya, as is taught.
410.nuance: The list runs from cosmic bodies to the inner faculties, so that both the outer world and the mind come from one material source.

links.note: The Kural says the world has the Primal Lord as its first, as letters have 'a'; Tirumular says one alone creates, protects and removes the worlds. The Kural names only primacy; Tirumular spells it out as the three acts.

Both speak of the one who made the world. The Kural, conditionally, curses him if he meant some to live by begging; Tirumular praises him without reserve. Because the Kural's curse is conditional, this is a difference of attitude, not a contradiction.
The same quatrain twice, with ஓராயமே (one host) in place of ஒருவனுமே (one alone): if ஆயம் is the assembled powers, the second recasts the one agent as a company.
386 gives creation to one He and one She with five sons; 404 to one alone. Read with 396 and 401, the She is his Shakti, so the two agree that the agent is one.
386 names the pair who create; 396 says what their creating is: play that bears fruit in every season.
382 has bindu rise from nada and the will; 1923 lists what unfolds from bindu as it rises: kundalini, the gods, the powers and speech.
Both make the bindu of Maya the source of everything: 410 by listing sun, moon, elements, speech and mind, 1930 by calling bindu the cause in all its effects, as clay in a pot.
1927 gives the five acts to the Supreme; 398 says the five lords who carry them out are born of bindu and still bound by anava. The acts are his, the agents are not.

source_issues: 406 and 414 are nearly the same verse (கூடும் பிறவிக் in 406, கூடு மரபிற் in 414, and 414's variant restores கூடும்பிறவிக்); one is probably a duplicate.
404 and 407 are the same quatrain with ஒருவனுமே and ஓராயமே; ஓராயமே may be a corruption.
405: the variant last line ஐந்தார் பிறவி அமைத்து நின்றானே reverses the sense of the received அந்தார் பிறவி அறுத்துநின் றானே.
399: the count of parts (முப்பால், ஒன்று, மற்றைய மூன்று) does not add up as read.
385: கான் and தேன் do not fit the expected sequence of elements and may be corrupt.
